Hello,

I am the debugging agent, and I've analyzed the build failure for the `kripke` application. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Analysis

The build process fails during the `make` command with a generic `Error 2`. The build log shows that the failure occurs after it has successfully built several targets, specifically after attempting to link an example from one of Kripke's submodules (`ex3_colored-indexset_solution`).

The root cause of the issue is that the default `make` command attempts to build the `all` target, which includes all executables defined in the project, including the examples from its dependencies. The build is failing on one of these non-essential examples. We only need the main `kripke` executable, not the examples from its submodules.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we should modify the build command to specifically build and install only the main `kripke` application, bypassing the problematic examples. The Kripke build system provides a standard `install` target which is configured to build the `kripke` binary and copy it to a system path (`/usr/local/bin` by default).

By replacing the `make && cp` sequence with `make install`, we can achieve a more robust build that only compiles and installs the necessary components.

Please apply the following change to the `Dockerfile`:

```diff
--- a/Dockerfile
+++ b/Dockerfile
@@ -47,9 +47,8 @@
       -D KRIPKE_USE_OPENMP=ON \
       .. && \
     # Build the application using all available processor cores
-    make -j$(nproc) && \
-    # Copy the kripke executable to a standard location in the PATH
-    cp bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
+    # Build and install the kripke target, which avoids building failing examples
+    make -j$(nproc) install && \
     # Clean up the build source to reduce final image size
     rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}
 

```

This single change will instruct the build system to only create and install the `kripke` binary, which should resolve the build failure.

# Use a standard Ubuntu base image suitable for CPU builds
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, Git, certificates, and Open MPI
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized/cloud environments
# - Exclude loopback and docker network interfaces to prevent MPI from using them for communication.
# - Allow oversubscription of processes, which is useful for running on a single node or in CI/CD.
# - Disable a shared memory mechanism that can cause issues in some container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_exclude=lo,docker0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set build-time arguments for repository and branch
ARG KRIPKE_REPO_URL=https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git
ARG KRIPKE_BRANCH=main
ARG BUILD_DIR=/tmp/kripke_build

# Clone, compile, and install the Kripke application
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size
RUN mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    # Clone the specified branch of the Kripke repository
    git clone --depth 1 --branch ${KRIPKE_BRANCH} ${KRIPKE_REPO_URL} . && \
    # Create a build directory
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake for a release build with MPI and OpenMP
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D KRIPKE_USE_MPI=ON \
      -D KRIPKE_USE_OPENMP=ON \
      .. && \
    # Build the application using all available processor cores
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the kripke executable to a standard location in the PATH
    cp bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the build source to reduce final image size
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default working directory for the container

# Set the entrypoint to the Kripke executable

# Provide a default command (e.g., to show help) if no arguments are given

I am the debugging agent, and I've analyzed the build failure for the `kripke` application. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Analysis

The build process fails during the `make` command with a generic `Error 2`. The build log shows that the failure occurs after it has successfully built several targets, specifically after attempting to link an example from one of Kripke's submodules (`ex3_colored-indexset_solution`).

The root cause of the issue is that the default `make` command attempts to build the `all` target, which includes all executables defined in the project, including the examples from its dependencies. The build is failing on one of these non-essential examples. We only need the main `kripke` executable, not the examples from its submodules.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we should modify the build command to specifically build and install only the main `kripke` application, bypassing the problematic examples. The Kripke build system provides a standard `install` target which is configured to build the `kripke` binary and copy it to a system path (`/usr/local/bin` by default).

By replacing the `make && cp` sequence with `make install`, we can achieve a more robust build that only compiles and installs the necessary components.

Please apply the following change to the `Dockerfile`:

```diff
--- a/Dockerfile
+++ b/Dockerfile
@@ -47,9 +47,8 @@
       -D KRIPKE_USE_OPENMP=ON \
       .. && \
     # Build the application using all available processor cores
-    make -j$(nproc) && \
-    # Copy the kripke executable to a standard location in the PATH

+    # Build and install the kripke target, which avoids building failing examples

     # Clean up the build source to reduce final image size

```

### Error Analysis

The build process fails during the `make` command with a generic `Error 2`. The build log shows that the failure occurs after it has successfully built several targets, specifically after attempting to link an example from one of Kripke's submodules (`ex3_colored-indexset_solution`).

The root cause of the issue is that the default `make` command attempts to build the `all` target, which includes all executables defined in the project, including the examples from its dependencies. The build is failing on one of these non-essential examples. We only need the main `kripke` executable, not the examples from its submodules.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we should modify the build command to specifically build and install only the main `kripke` application, bypassing the problematic examples. The Kripke build system provides a standard `install` target which is configured to build the `kripke` binary and copy it to a system path (`/usr/local/bin` by default).

By replacing the `make && cp` sequence with `make install`, we can achieve a more robust build that only compiles and installs the necessary components.

Please apply the following change to the `Dockerfile`:

```diff
--- a/Dockerfile
+++ b/Dockerfile
@@ -47,9 +47,8 @@
       -D KRIPKE_USE_OPENMP=ON \
       .. && \

-    # Copy the kripke executable to a standard location in the PATH

+    # Build and install the kripke target, which avoids building failing examples

```

Hello,

I am the debugging agent, and I've analyzed the build failure for the `kripke` application. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Analysis

The build process fails during the `make` command with a generic `Error 2`. The build log shows that the failure occurs after it has successfully built several targets, specifically after attempting to link an example from one of Kripke's submodules (`ex3_colored-indexset_solution`).

The root cause of the issue is that the default `make` command attempts to build the `all` target, which includes all executables defined in the project, including the examples from its dependencies. The build is failing on one of these non-essential examples. We only need the main `kripke` executable, not the examples from its submodules.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we should modify the build command to specifically build and install only the main `kripke` application, bypassing the problematic examples. The Kripke build system provides a standard `install` target which is configured to build the `kripke` binary and copy it to a system path (`/usr/local/bin` by default).

By replacing the `make && cp` sequence with `make install`, we can achieve a more robust build that only compiles and installs the necessary components.

Please apply the following change to the `Dockerfile`:

```diff
--- a/Dockerfile
+++ b/Dockerfile
@@ -47,9 +47,8 @@
       -D KRIPKE_USE_OPENMP=ON \
       .. && \
     # Build the application using all available processor cores
-    make -j$(nproc) && \
-    # Copy the kripke executable to a standard location in the PATH
-    cp bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
+    # Build and install the kripke target, which avoids building failing examples
+    make -j$(nproc) install && \
     # Clean up the build source to reduce final image size

Hello,

I am the debugging agent, and I've analyzed the build failure for the `kripke` application. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Analysis

The build process fails during the `make` command with a generic `Error 2`. The build log shows that the failure occurs after it has successfully built several targets, specifically after attempting to link an example from one of Kripke's submodules (`ex3_colored-indexset_solution`).

The root cause of the issue is that the default `make` command attempts to build the `all` target, which includes all executables defined in the project, including the examples from its dependencies. The build is failing on one of these non-essential examples. We only need the main `kripke` executable, not the examples from its submodules.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we should modify the build command to specifically build and install only the main `kripke` application, bypassing the problematic examples. The Kripke build system provides a standard `install` target which is configured to build the `kripke` binary and copy it to a system path (`/usr/local/bin` by default).

By replacing the `make && cp` sequence with `make install`, we can achieve a more robust build that only compiles and installs the necessary components.

Please apply the following change to the `Dockerfile`:

```diff
--- a/Dockerfile
+++ b/Dockerfile
@@ -47,9 +47,8 @@
       -D KRIPKE_USE_OPENMP=ON \
       .. && \
     # Build the application using all available processor cores
-    make -j$(nproc) && \
-    # Copy the kripke executable to a standard location in the PATH
-    cp bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
+    # Build and install the kripke target, which avoids building failing examples
+    make -j$(nproc) install && \
     # Clean up the build source to reduce final image size
     rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}
 

```

This single change will instruct the build system to only create and install the `kripke` binary, which should resolve the build failure.

I am the debugging agent, and I've analyzed the build failure for the `kripke` application. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Analysis

The build process fails during the `make` command with a generic `Error 2`. The build log shows that the failure occurs after it has successfully built several targets, specifically after attempting to link an example from one of Kripke's submodules (`ex3_colored-indexset_solution`).

The root cause of the issue is that the default `make` command attempts to build the `all` target, which includes all executables defined in the project, including the examples from its dependencies. The build is failing on one of these non-essential examples. We only need the main `kripke` executable, not the examples from its submodules.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we should modify the build command to specifically build and install only the main `kripke` application, bypassing the problematic examples. The Kripke build system provides a standard `install` target which is configured to build the `kripke` binary and copy it to a system path (`/usr/local/bin` by default).

By replacing the `make && cp` sequence with `make install`, we can achieve a more robust build that only compiles and installs the necessary components.

Please apply the following change to the `Dockerfile`:

```diff
--- a/Dockerfile
+++ b/Dockerfile
@@ -47,9 +47,8 @@
       -D KRIPKE_USE_OPENMP=ON \
       .. && \
     # Build the application using all available processor cores
-    make -j$(nproc) && \
-    # Copy the kripke executable to a standard location in the PATH
-    cp bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
+    # Build and install the kripke target, which avoids building failing examples
+    make -j$(nproc) install && \
     # Clean up the build source to reduce final image size
     rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}
 

```

This single change will instruct the build system to only create and install the `kripke` binary, which should resolve the build failure.

FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, Git, certificates, and Open MPI
# gfortran is included as it is a common dependency for linking against Open MPI
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce final image size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized/cloud environments like Kubernetes
# - Exclude loopback and docker network interfaces to prevent MPI from using them for communication.
# - Allow oversubscription of processes, useful for dense node packing.
# - Disable a shared memory mechanism that can cause issues in some container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_exclude=lo,docker0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set build-time arguments for repository and branch for flexibility
ARG KRIPKE_REPO_URL=https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git
ARG KRIPKE_BRANCH=main
ARG BUILD_DIR=/tmp/kripke_build

# Clone, compile, and install the Kripke application in a single RUN layer
# This optimizes image size by containing all build artifacts in one layer that can be cleaned up.
RUN mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    # Clone the specified branch recursively to fetch required submodules (e.g., BLT build system).
    git clone --recursive --depth 1 --branch ${KRIPKE_BRANCH} ${KRIPKE_REPO_URL} . && \
    # Create a separate build directory
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake for a release build with MPI and OpenMP enabled
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D KRIPKE_USE_MPI=ON \
      -D KRIPKE_USE_OPENMP=ON \
      .. && \
    # Build the application using all available processor cores
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the kripke executable to a standard location on the PATH
    cp bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the build source directory to reduce final image size
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default working directory for the container for user data or input files
WORKDIR /data

# Set the entrypoint to the Kripke executable
ENTRYPOINT ["kripke"]

# Provide a default command (e.g., to show help) if the container is run without arguments
CMD ["--help"]

The root cause of the issue is that the default `make` command attempts to build the `all` target, which includes all executables defined in the project, including the examples from its dependencies. To resolve this, we should modify the build command to specifically build and install only the main `kripke` application, bypassing the problematic examples. Hello,

I am the debugging agent, and I've analyzed the build failure for the `kripke` application. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Analysis

The build process fails during the `make` command with a generic `Error 2`. The build log shows that the failure occurs after it has successfully built several targets, specifically after attempting to link an example from one of Kripke's submodules (`ex3_colored-indexset_solution`).

The root cause of the issue is that the default `make` command attempts to build the `all` target, which includes all executables defined in the project, including the examples from its dependencies. The build is failing on one of these non-essential examples. We only need the main `kripke` executable, not the examples from its submodules.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we should modify the build command to specifically build and install only the main `kripke` application, bypassing the problematic examples. The Kripke build system provides a standard `install` target which is configured to build the `kripke` binary and copy it to a system path (`/usr/local/bin` by default).

By replacing the `make && cp` sequence with `make install`, we can achieve a more robust build that only compiles and installs the necessary components.

Please apply the following change to the `Dockerfile`:

```diff
--- a/Dockerfile
+++ b/Dockerfile
@@ -47,9 +47,8 @@
       -D KRIPKE_USE_OPENMP=ON \
       .. && \
     # Build the application using all available processor cores
-    make -j$(nproc) && \
-    # Copy the kripke executable to a standard location in the PATH
-    cp bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
+    # Build and install the kripke target, which avoids building failing examples
+    make -j$(nproc) install && \
     # Clean up the build source to reduce final image size
     rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}
 

```

This single change will instruct the build system to only create and install the `kripke` binary, which should resolve the build failure.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, you need to change the default value for the `KRIPKE_BRANCH` argument from `main` to `master`. This will ensure the `git clone` command targets the correct branch.

Here is the corrected Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
# Use a standard Ubuntu base image suitable for CPU builds
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, Git, certificates, and Open MPI
# gfortran is included as it is a common dependency for linking against Open MPI
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce final image size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized/cloud environments like Kubernetes
# - Exclude loopback and docker network interfaces to prevent MPI from using them for communication.
# - Allow oversubscription of processes, useful for dense node packing.
# - Disable a shared memory mechanism that can cause issues in some container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_exclude=lo,docker0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set build-time arguments for repository and branch for flexibility
ARG KRIPKE_REPO_URL=https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git
ARG KRIPKE_BRANCH=master
ARG BUILD_DIR=/tmp/kripke_build

# Clone, compile, and install the Kripke application in a single RUN layer
# This optimizes image size by containing all build artifacts in one layer that is cleaned up.
RUN mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    # Clone the specified branch recursively to fetch required submodules (e.g., BLT build system).
    git clone --recursive --depth 1 --branch ${KRIPKE_BRANCH} ${KRIPKE_REPO_URL} . && \
    # Create a separate build directory as per standard CMake practice
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake for a release build with MPI and OpenMP enabled
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D KRIPKE_USE_MPI=ON \
      -D KRIPKE_USE_OPENMP=ON \
      .. && \
    # Build the application using all available processor cores
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the kripke executable to a standard location on the PATH
    cp bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the build source directory to reduce final image size
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# Set a default working directory for the container for user data or input files
WORKDIR /data

# Set the entrypoint to the Kripke executable, making the container behave like the app
ENTRYPOINT ["kripke"]

# Provide a default command (e.g., to show help) if the container is run without arguments
CMD ["--help"]
```
